title: Poby: SmartNIC-accelerated Image Provisioning for Coldstart in Clouds
problem: Cloud VM coldstart latency is dominated by image provisioning—transferring and decompressing large VM images from storage to compute nodes consumes CPU cycles and network bandwidth, delaying instance availability.
motivation: Fast coldstart is critical for cloud elasticity and cost efficiency, enabling rapid scaling and improving resource utilization in cloud platforms.
method: Poby uses SmartNICs—specialized hardware cards positioned in the network between storage and compute nodes—to handle image decompression and transfer. The SmartNIC's hardware acceleration decompresses the VM image and moves it from storage to the compute node, work that would otherwise use the compute node's CPU. By offloading this work, Poby frees the CPU for other tasks, reducing contention and speeding up image provisioning.
key_novelty: The innovation is using a SmartNIC (a specialized network acceleration card) to handle VM image decompression and transfer instead of relying on the compute node's CPU.
contributions: SmartNIC-based architecture for accelerating cloud image provisioning
Hardware acceleration of image decompression in the network datapath
Reduced VM coldstart latency demonstrated in cloud environments
System design integrating SmartNIC acceleration with cloud provisioning workflows
limitations: Not discussed based on title alone.
primary_theme: SmartNIC acceleration for cloud VM provisioning
